meta.why: Symptoms are interpreted in context. Exploring what increases or decreases a sense of threat can support a more informed conversation and plan.

hero.title: Protection, Context, and Safety
hero.subtitle: Look for patterns without diagnosing yourself
hero.description: Pain is a real protective experience influenced by many kinds of information. Context can matter, but no checklist can determine by itself whether a symptom is safe or dangerous.

tiles.title: **Seek timely assessment**
content: Significant trauma or unexplained systemic illness
New neurological changes or loss of function
Symptoms that concern you or do not fit your usual pattern

tiles.title: **Notice context**
content: What you were doing when symptoms changed
Sleep, stress, health, and recent activity
What you expected or feared might happen
Which modifications improved comfort or function

tiles.title: **Avoid simple rules**
content: Pain severity is not a precise damage meter
Pain improving with movement does not prove nothing is wrong
No swelling does not automatically prove an activity is safe
One difficult response does not always mean lasting harm

tiles.title: **Build an informed plan**
content: Discuss uncertainty or concerning changes with your clinician
Use gradual, individualized activity when appropriate
Track function and participation as well as symptoms
Adjust the plan using your response and clinical guidance

microAction.title: Context Check
microAction.description: Choose a familiar activity already considered appropriate for you. Note your confidence, the dose you tried, your response, and any question you want to discuss. Do not use this activity to test a new or concerning symptom.
